summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 5 upside misses — WDC +15%, DASH +12%, STX +8%, COHR +8%, CVNA +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (FOXA -17%, FOX -15%, CBOE -9%, MPWR -7%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: FOXA (-16.84%) — Fox Corp announced a $22B acquisition of streaming platform Roku at a 34% premium in a cash-and-stock deal adding ~$8.3B debt and heavy shareholder dilution — market punished the acquirer. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe. FOXA is a large-cap legacy media name unlikely screened by momentum or mean-reversion filters. The -16% move was a classic acquirer-discount gap on an M&A announcement; capturing it requires short capability and pre-announcement news-reactive positioning no current strategy holds

top_movers.catalyst: Morgan Stanley raised WDC price target 33% ($488→$650) on June 15 after-hours, projecting AI-driven HDD demand of 40-50% annually vs. 30-35% supply through 2028, lifting 2028 EPS estimates 70% above consensus.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. WDC is a large-cap AI storage hardware name; the catalyst (MS analyst PT hike, published after-hours June 15) produced a ~15% pre-open gap that would exceed most momentum gap filters even if the ticker were eligible.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an analyst-upgrade catalyst gate: for AI hardware names (HDD/SSD) with a ≥20% sell-side PT hike published after-hours, trigger long entry at open if pre-market gap is +5% to +12%; exclude gaps above that threshold to avoid overshoot risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Trump Administration announced a peace deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz; falling oil prices and Treasury yields compressed discount rates, lifting consumer-internet valuations and signalling improved ad-spend and discretionary demand outlook for DoorDash.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. The move was a macro/geopolitical second-order effect — oil-yield compression rippling into consumer internet — not a company-specific signal; no pre-market fundamental screen flags this type of sector-wide re-rating.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a macro-trigger overlay: when WTI drops >3% and 10-yr yield falls >8bps intraday, expand the momentum strategy's universe to include watchlisted consumer-internet names (e.g. DASH, SNAP) gating on gap-up ≥+3% at open to confirm direction.

top_movers.catalyst: Multiple bulge-bracket analysts (TD Cowen →$1,500, RBC →$1,200) raised price targets on the same session citing record AI-driven HBM/DRAM demand, lifting MU ~10.8% ahead of June 24 fiscal Q3 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: MU is outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded by a sector or name-list filter not yet updated for AI-era semiconductor mega-caps. Analyst upgrade cascades materialise pre-market, requiring positioning before post-open signals can trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a coordinated-upgrade trigger to news-reactive that fires within 30 min of open when ≥2 tier-1 firms raise targets ≥15% on the same session, with a temporary universe waiver for large-cap semiconductor names.

top_movers.catalyst: U.S. Commerce Dept signed a $50M CHIPS Act letter of intent with COHR to expand its 6-inch Indium Phosphide fab in Sherman TX, doubling production space and quadrupling wafer capacity.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. COHR is a ~$81B large-cap photonics/semiconductor name; the +7.75% move was driven by a government-funding announcement (CHIPS Act LOI) disclosed pre-market — not derivable from prior-session technical signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Maintain a watchlist of semiconductor names with pending CHIPS Act applications; add a news-reactive entry rule that buys at open when a CHIPS Act LOI ≥$25M is confirmed in pre-market headlines for any watchlist name.

top_movers.catalyst: CNBC June 16 feature revealed Carvana's quiet expansion into new-vehicle franchises (7 Stellantis dealerships acquired since 2025); one store hit 700+ units/month, becoming Stellantis' top-volume US dealer.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. Catalyst was a qualitative CNBC narrative piece — not an earnings beat or hard data — difficult to flag pre-open via structured news signals. Day's volume (3.85M vs 10M avg) would also fail most momentum strategies' volume floor filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a media-feature flag for major-outlet (CNBC/Bloomberg) stories on business-model pivots; gate entry requiring ≥0.5× prior-session avg volume at open to avoid chasing low-volume narrative pops into names not otherwise in the universe.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. FOXA is a large-cap legacy media name unlikely screened by momentum or mean-reversion filters. The -16% move was a classic acquirer-discount gap on an M&A announcement; capturing it requires short capability and pre-announcement news-reactive positioning no current strategy holds
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — capturing acquirer-discount gaps requires short capability and a deal-announcement event trigger the bot does not have; adding FOXA to a long-only universe would not have helped here)

top_movers.catalyst: Fox Corp announced a $22B acquisition of Roku at a 34% premium (cash+stock), adding ~$8.3B in debt and significant shareholder dilution — classic acquirer-discount sell-off.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. FOX is a large-cap media/entertainment name not currently covered; the drop was M&A-catalyst-driven (acquirer discount on announcement day), a move type that requires short capability and intraday news-reactive entry — neither typically available in long-only momentum or mean-rev
top_movers.suggestion: Add FOX/FOXA to a news-reactive watchlist with an 'large-deal acquirer' signal: flag for short entry when announced deal-value exceeds 30% of acquirer market-cap at >25% premium; only actionable if short capability is enabled, otherwise mark as (no-op — long-only constraint).

top_movers.catalyst: Tentative US-Iran peace deal compressed the VIX sharply, threatening CBOE's volatility-dependent options revenue; a rival-exchange SpaceX equity options launch on the same day added market-share pressure.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CBOE is a large-cap exchange operator; its decline was driven by VIX collapse from a geopolitical surprise, which pre-market momentum and mean-reversion signals cannot anticipate.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'VIX-compression short' rule: when spot VIX drops ≥15% intraday, allow short entries in exchange operators (CBOE, ICE, CME) — but only if short capability exists; otherwise mark as no-op.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide de-risking of high-multiple semiconductors on global rate jitters; investors reduced exposure to elevated-P/E AI chip names — no company-specific catalyst, macro-driven pullback.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. MPWR (~$72B market cap) is a high-multiple semiconductor name; the -7% drop was macro-driven sector de-risking on rate jitters, not a technical or earnings signal bot filters would have detected pre-trade.
top_movers.suggestion: Onboard large-cap semis (market cap > $30B) to an expanded universe; add a rate-sensitivity momentum-short sub-strategy triggered by 10yr yield ≥ +8bp intraday to capture sector-wide de-risk events like today's.
